human_tolerance.notes: Females carrying offspring stay in smaller areas and reduce their movements, so a garden with a woodpile or burrow can hold a female for months; the species is a common visitor to compost and refuse in Brazilian towns.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Litters average about six young; the young are weaned after roughly 100 days and females become sexually mature at about 193 days, so pouch young and newly independent animals appear across the warm and wet season.

vocalizations.description: A loud, repeated, rasping screech with the mouth open, given by a disturbed animal at close range; opossums are usually silent and are heard more often than seen.
A soft chittering or muttering when two animals meet, especially a female with young.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2439928 and iNaturalist taxon id 42657, as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API and given in issue #47.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese 'gamba-de-orelha-grande' from the article's interlanguage links and the article's own alternative names sarue and gamba.

range.note: Wikipedia: found in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay.

traits.mass_kg.note: PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 1105.88 and EltonTraits MamFuncDat BodyMass-Value 1163.99 g, which agree to within 5%.

traits.length_m.note: No openly licensed source gives a head-body or total length for this species. Derived by scaling the Virginia opossum record in this repository (0.69 m total at 2.25 kg) by the cube root of the mass ratio, 1.106/2.25: a 1.1 kg animal is about 0.55 m nose to tail tip. Authored, not a published measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No openly licensed source states a wild lifespan for this species. Authored as a low-precision value typical of a small marsupial, close to the Virginia opossum figure this repository uses (2 y); it is a judgement, not a measurement.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat Diet-Vunk 30, Diet-Scav 30, Diet-Inv 20, Diet-PlantO 20 (plant other mapped to browse).

traits.social.note: PanTHERIA records no SocialGrpSize for this species and opossums are solitary outside the breeding season; Solitary [1, 1] is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits MamFuncDat Activity-Nocturnal 1 with diurnal and crepuscular both 0, and PanTHERIA ActivityCycle 1 (nocturnal); the species name itself is used for the broad-eared nocturnal opossum.

traits.defense.note: Authored: freezes, then gapes and screeches rather than fleeing; opossums are famously unresponsive and hiss or scream when threatened.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Strictly nocturnal and quick to withdraw into cover, so set high.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk and Trot chosen: a ground-moving nocturnal marsupial that trots when disturbed. Neither has an arachnid or climbing mode, and it does not fly.

traits.skin.note: Fur, with a sparsely haired tail.

traits.flight.note: Fur, with a sparsely haired tail.

traits.respiration.note: Fur, with a sparsely haired tail.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None; a marsupial with a short pouch life.

traits.perching.note: Climbs low but does not perch like a bird; set to false.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement: shelters by day in a burrow, hollow log or under dense cover rather than building a nest, so Burrow is the honest value.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value 'S' (surface), which with a small arboreal share for climbing low vegetation gives ground 0.75 / arboreal 0.25, the same split as the Virginia opossum record in this repository.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: shelters by day in a burrow, hollow log or under dense cover, so burrow is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the burrow shelter weight is judgement, as no open source ranks its relative importance.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: females carrying offspring tend to stay in smaller areas and reduce their movements.

seasonal.strategy.note: Tropical and subtropical species active year round; no dormancy or migration described.

seasonal.phases.note: Litter size, weaning age and sexual maturity from PanTHERIA; the calendar windows are judgements placing pouch young across the warm, wet season.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration from the weaning and maturity ages in PanTHERIA; scale is authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored params for the shared ground-forager program. A small flee distance and a Trot flee gait match a slow, close-range nocturnal animal that freezes; rest_sun_lo_deg/rest_sun_hi_deg left at 10/90, the program's nocturnal setting.

look.note: Colours from the species' appearance (grey-brown grizzled dorsal fur, cream face and underside, large pale ears with dark rims, dark eye mask, pale feet and a sparsely haired tail); proportions authored on the didelphis-virginiana template with a shorter tail, and the mask, ear-rim and tail-base extra parts render the big pale ears and bare tail that give the species its name.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Authored geometry estimate for the required quadruped field, following the convention of the Virginia opossum record in this repository: a short-legged shoulder height set to about 39% of head-body length, here 0.13 m against a derived head-body length of about 0.33 m.

traits.senses.note: Authored from the species' biology: colour vision plus strong night vision for a strictly nocturnal forager, with both smell and hearing acute. No open source quantifies them here.

vocalizations.screech.note: Descriptions follow the opossum literature the Wikipedia article cites; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them. No open source gives a frequency band, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.chitter.note: Descriptions follow the opossum literature the Wikipedia article cites; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them. No open source gives a frequency band, so freq_hz is omitted.
